verdict: AppLovin's advertising platform grew revenue 91% from a year ago to $678M and kept a 54% operating margin, while the apps business it later sold lost $23M — total net income was $236M.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $74M on AppLovin's debt, partly offset by $2M of other income, net — plus a $23M loss from the apps business AppLovin sold in June 2025, which accounting rules report as discontinued operations: a net $95M expense.
follow100Note: The 'other expense' step nets $74M of interest expense against $2M of other income, and includes the $23M loss from the sold apps business. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: The platform nearly doubled
takeaways.text: Continuing revenue rose 91% from a year ago to $678M — up from $355M of software-platform revenue in Q1 2023 — as AXON, AppLovin's AI ad engine, kept finding better matches between advertisers and app users.

takeaways.title: A 54% operating margin
takeaways.text: The continuing platform turned $678M of revenue into $364M of operating income. Its total costs were just $314M — they barely grow with sales, so most of each new revenue dollar drops through to profit.

takeaways.title: Continuing profit beat the headline
takeaways.text: Profit from continuing operations was $259M — more than the reported $236M of net income, because the apps business AppLovin later sold lost $23M in the quarter. Operating cash flow was $393M and free cash flow $388M.

footerNote: AppLovin reports as a single segment. The flow shows the continuing advertising-platform business, as restated after the apps business was sold in June 2025: the Q1 2024 continuing figures come from the six months ended June 30, 2024 in AppLovin's Q2 2025 Form 10-Q, less the Q2 2024 quarter. The apps business's $23M loss is folded into the 'other' step so the bottom line matches the reported net income of $236M; the continuing platform itself earned $259M. When Q1 was first reported in May 2024, the apps business was still included and total revenue was $1,058M.
